Serverless data pipelines have a very dynamic, non-stationary workload, bursty request patterns, cold-start delays, and resource variability are the order of the day, and traditional one-dimensional or statical optimization strategies do not apply. Serverless data pipelines have a very dynamic, non-stationary workload, bursty request patterns, cold-start delays, and resource variability are the order of the day, and traditional one-dimensional or statical optimization strategies do not apply. The currently used methods mainly aim at minimizing either cost or latency without paying much attention to predictive uncertainty and its effects on the stability of the decision making which results in suboptimal and unstable scheduling in real world situations. In a bid to fill this gap, this paper introduces a new multi-objective framework called ERUO (Entropy-Regularized Uncertainty-Aware Optimization) that concurrently optimizes the latency, cost, probability of cold-start, and uncertainty in a single reinforcement learning framework. ERUO proposes to use an entropy-based regularization on predictive uncertainty distributions to allow the system to discourage unstable regimes of decisions and enhance resistance to workload variability. The structure combines the use of quantile-based uncertainty modelling, gradient-boosted prediction, LSTM-based workload forecasting and PPO-based policy optimizer. As shown by experimental assessment on real-world cloud traces (Alibaba and Google cluster datasets), ERUO can make latency, cost, and cold-start instances reductions of up to 23.6, 18.4 and 27.1 over baseline approaches, as well as converge faster and can make improved decisions. The importance of this work is that uncertainty entropy has been formally coupled with the control optimization, which offers an efficient and scalable solution to managing next-generation serverless data pipelines.

\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-9382021/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 4, 14]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.36227/techrxiv.177006117.78624713/v1\", \"title\": [\"DeepFlow: A Multi-Objective Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Real-Time Pedagogical Adaptation in Serious Games\"], \"abstract\": \"The integration of Serious Games and Massive Multiplayer Online RolePlaying Games (MMORPGs) into Computer Science curricula offers a promising avenue for enhancing student engagement and fostering Computational Thinking (CT). However, existing educational MMORPGs predominantly rely on static difficulty curves and heuristic-based scaffolding. This rigidity often fails to accommodate the heterogeneous cognitive profiles of learners, leading to violations of Flow Theory conditions, specifically inducing boredom in advanced students or anxiety in novices. This paper introduces DeepFlow, a novel Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent directly within the game loop of a generic educational MMORPG architecture. The system aims to function as an autonomous ”Digital Tutor,” dynamically tailoring the learning experience to the individual’s Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD). We formulate the pedagogical adaptation problem as a Multi-Objective Markov Decision Process (MOMDP), where the agent optimizes two conflicting objectives: maximizing learning gains (Concept Mastery) and sustaining engagement (Flow State). Utilizing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with a specialized reward function derived from Item Response Theory (IRT) and Cognitive Load Theory, DeepFlow dynamically adjusts quest complexity, hint granularity, and narrative urgency in real-time. A comprehensive simulation-based evaluation involving varied learner profiles demonstrated that DeepFlow significantly reduces projected attrition rates and improves code comprehension metrics compared to static baselines. Furthermore, behavioral analysis reveals that the DRL agent autonomously discovers complex scaffolding strategies, such as ”fading support,” akin to expert human tutors. While learning gains were positive, we observed that the PPO agent  struggled to converge for ’Chaotic’ profiles (agents initialized with random noise), often oscillating between hint levels before stabilizing. This suggests the reward function may need further tuning for highly unpredictable student behaviors. Conclusion: These findings suggest that neuro-adaptive agents can effectively bridge the ”ScalabilityAdaptivity” gap in game-based learning, offering a scalable path toward personalized education.\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.177006117.78624713/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 2, 2]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.52202/085713-3600\", \"title\": [\"Sharp Analysis for KL-Regularized Contextual Bandits and RLHF\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-3600\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "97d0bb3e416e641e041f9b0431c42d77bbf2be7bcf3cbc74aa028ad80b135384", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.5990578", "doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-9382021/v1", "doi:10.36227/techrxiv.177006117.78624713/v1", "doi:10.52202/085713-3600"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5990578", "https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-9382021/v1", "https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.177006117.78624713/v1", "https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-3600"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
